cohort: The study included 662 couples with only low-grade blastocysts who underwent freeze-thaw blastocyst transfer at a single reproductive center.
finding: Paternal age, maternal basal luteinizing hormone level, endometrial preparation scheme, and blastocyst development days were identified as independent factors affecting low-grade blastocyst freeze-thaw transfer outcomes, with advanced paternal age and high maternal basal LH adversely affecting live birth, while artificial cycle preparation and day 5 blastocyst selection improved the probability of live birth.
